title: Decide how app-target logic gets tested at all
acceptance: A decision on where tests for app-target code live: an iOS unit test target, a second local SPM package for pure app logic, or an accepted permanent gap
If a test target: the cost to the gate is measured, since an iOS test target needs a booted simulator and D-0001 chose SPM precisely to avoid that
ReaderContrastAudit is wired into whatever is chosen, so the palette cannot regress silently
notes: Surfaced by /code-review on T-0014: ReaderContrastAudit is unreferenced dead code because there is nowhere in the app target to run it from. D-0001 solved testing for the extractor by moving it to Packages/SwiftReadability, and that was right for the gate — but it left every app-target type (Palette, ReaderTheme, LibraryFilter, LibraryIndex, Post) with zero test coverage and no way to acquire any. The factory will keep hitting this: any task whose acceptance says 'and it cannot regress' is currently unsatisfiable for app code. Note the tension — an iOS test target reintroduces the simulator dependency that makes the gate slow and serial, which is exactly what D-0001 escaped.
